name: Imidapril
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Imidapril is an ACE inhibitor whose active metabolite is excreted in urine. The Singapore product information starts at 2.5 mg once daily in kidney impairment and, at creatinine clearance (CrCl) below 30 mL/min or serum creatinine above 3 mg/dL, advises halving the dose or extending the interval because accumulation can cause hypotension and further kidney decline. Hemodialysis with AN69 membranes is contraindicated. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: Singapore product information uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min) or serum creatinine (above 3 mg/dL).
chip: CrCl <30: half dose or longer interval

bands.recommendation: Usual: 5 to 10 mg once daily (Singapore NDF).
Hypertension with kidney impairment: start 2.5 mg once daily and titrate (Singapore NDF). Monitor potassium and creatinine.

CrCl <30 mL/min (or serum creatinine above 3 mg/dL): use with care; consider halving the usual dose or extending the dosing interval. Start at 2.5 mg once daily in hypertension with kidney impairment (Singapore NDF). Monitor potassium and creatinine.

hd: Hemodialysis with AN69 (polyacrylonitrile) membranes is contraindicated (anaphylactoid reactions). Dose as for CrCl <30 (half dose or longer interval); no dialysis-specific dosing given (Singapore NDF).
pd: Dose as for CrCl <30; no PD-specific data.
crrt: No data; avoid starting ACE inhibitors in acute kidney injury.
monitoring: Potassium and creatinine after starting and dose changes; blood pressure (excess hypotension); angioedema (Singapore NDF).
